verdicts.why: The script supports it: Reed tells Ben the ship is 'just like the shuttle you flew', Ben says Johnny 'washed out of NASA', and Reed says Victor 'knew about NASA. Maybe he made the call to shut us down.' That is a past group the screen tells, so it goes first, keyed to his first title, under the dataset's existing name NASA.

In S3 episodes 4 and 6, Morgan heals and enthralls Robert with a crow necklace. Under her control he names her CEO of Wizard for the coven's Corvus plan, which is forced service and counts. Tina breaks the spell in episode 7 and he turns on the coven. He was never moved out of the Pride (the wiki lists him as a member who died), so ending back on The Pride matches Geoffrey's record.

In S3 episode 7, Geoffrey is enthralled through a crow necklace. He locks up Victor and Stacey 'under Morgan le Fay's orders' and holds the captured Runaways at Wizard, which is forced service to the coven. Dagger's light breaks the spell in episode 8, and in episode 9 he reassembles the Pride, which is already recorded. 'Morgan's coven' is the dataset's existing name.

Wikipedia S1: in episode 5 'Tandy applies as an intern at Roxxon Gulf to get close to the executives', and in episode 6 she 'becomes an intern for Mina' until Mina sees who she is. That is undercover service in the dataset's Roxxon. She then turns on Roxxon (confronts Scarborough, and in episode 10 Roxxon is exposed), so she ends Independent.
This is the left entry for item 20. Once she turns on Roxxon she leaves it for no group within Cloak & Dagger, the same format as Delgado's record.

On screen Erskine says only that he refused Hitler ('I am not interested'), that Hitler then 'sends the head of Hydra' after him, and that Schmidt took his unready serum. The film never shows or says that he worked for HYDRA. His forced work under Schmidt comes from the tie-in comic Captain America: First Vengeance, so this is an unsure case and the record stays as it is.

This Raft file covers Captain America: Civil War, where Bucky chooses cryo-sleep in Wakanda; Black Panther and Infinity War show him living there and fighting with Wakanda's forces. A person's hero and villain files list the same groups, and the twin A:bucky-barnes already has Wakanda at Civil War.

Hawkeye reveals S.H.I.E.L.D. as a past group: episode 4 ('their identity is still attached to that watch') and episode 6 (the watch with the S.H.I.E.L.D. logo and '19'). She was out of the agency before Age of Ultron. A past group is keyed to her first title, and nothing in Hawkeye moves her, so the stages are S.H.I.E.L.D. then Independent at Age of Ultron.
In Hawkeye she only helps by phone and gets her watch back, so she leaves no group there. Her only departure, from S.H.I.E.L.D., is at Age of Ultron.

In Black Panther Shuri says 'Everett Ross, former Air Force pilot, now CIA'. That is a past group the screen tells, so it is keyed to his first title, Captain America: Civil War, and goes before the CIA. As recorded, a Black Panther stage placed before a Civil War stage is out of story order.

Hawkeye episodes 2, 4 and 6 show Grills as a regular member of a LARP guild ('we're a guild'). It holds sessions in Central Park, has an organizer (Missy) and charges fees, and his video goes on its @newyorkcitylarpers page. That makes it an organization he belongs to, not a one-time job. 'NYC LARPers' is a plain name drawn from the screen ('the LARPers', the handle). He keeps FDNY.

Wikipedia: 'Shang-Chi, Xialing, Katy, Slattery, and Morris join the villagers in training'. Katy is armed with dragon-scale gear, taught archery by Guang Bo, and stands with Ta Lo's archers in the battle. That is the same service the dataset already records as Ta Lo for Trevor, Morris, Xialing and Shang-Chi.

Jon Jon is the ringmaster and announcer Xialing employs at her Golden Daggers Club, her right-hand man rather than a one-time hire. In the post-credits scene he stands at her side with Razor Fist as she takes over the Ten Rings. Both names already exist in the dataset (Xialing's record).

Episode 5 tells the Marine Corps service as a past group: he joined, was discharged, and then became a mercenary. A past group goes first. The National Art Gallery is Steven's job in the present, and the director fires him in episode 2, which is what the Independent stage stands for. The left entry stays 'Moon Knight'.

Episode 1 shows Akeya as leader of the Dora Milaje: Noni greets her as 'great leader of the Dora Milaje' and a Dora guard serves under her. The dataset records Dora Milaje members as Wakanda then The Dora Milaje (Okoye, Ayo), so the Wakanda stage stays, with the Dora Milaje added after it rather than replacing it.

In episode 1 Akeya picks Noni because she is an expelled soldier, and promises her place back in the Dora Milaje. Noni turns that down and joins the War Dogs (Hatut Zaraze). Wikipedia calls her 'a disgraced former member of the Dora Milaje'. A past group the screen tells goes first, and being expelled is the move to the Wakanda stage. (Side note: her step says 'In episode 2', but this is episode 1.)

held: minor employer. Her candy and book shop is a single minor job, seen once (Ironheart episode 4), which is an open owner question. Until the owner decides, the record stands: she left Kamar-Taj to raise Zelma, so it stays Masters of the Mystic Arts then Independent, with the left entry at Ironheart.
